title: Pyramid — precise decisions, efficient execution and trustworthy observation

intent.statement: Engineers and agents can understand, execute and verify Pyramid work with less avoidable overhead: trustworthy status and evidence, genuinely scoped runtime responses, precise workflow triggers, and a reusable project-aware goal prompt. Deliver A, B, C and the goal-prompt capability on dev/improvement while dogfooding installed 4.1; qualify the completed candidate before a safe local merge to main.

success_evidence.description: An engineer can distinguish recorded acceptance, present proof eligibility and publication health, inspect actual claim evidence, and receive lifecycle-correct next actions.
Agents obtain decision-complete scoped responses and use precise read, validation, refresh, proof-reuse and escalation triggers with measurable bounded overhead.
The default Observer explains proven outcomes, current work, consequential blockers, next actions and evidence at desktop/narrow widths with a consistent accessible visual grammar.
A discoverable project-aware goal-prompt skill drafts concise continuation prompts from current intent, harness and boundaries without inventing tools, authority or cleanup eligibility.

All improvements preserve canonical correctness, current proof, failed evidence, authority and both-host packaging; use installed 4.1 for dogfooding, qualify the candidate, then reconcile and merge locally.

constraints: Preserve canonical schemas/guards/history/ownership and all original acceptance, failure and assurance requirements. Use supported installed 4.1 interfaces for this intent; never hand-edit canonical state.
Keep task authority, source identity, external environment identity and reviewed procedure source separate. No proof may be made current by changing a post-run fingerprint.
Keep installed Codex/Claude plugins and their configuration unchanged until the owner separately requests an upgrade. Candidate-source success is not installed-host qualification.
Use scoped supporting context; complete required skill reads still apply. Preserve decision-critical fields and visible omissions; bytes/time are not model tokens.
Reuse existing Python and browser harnesses and immutable dependencies. Add only outcome-required observation capability; never substitute fixture pass values for performed execution or image review.

Main remains the preserved primary checkout. The new worktree is the only active development authority after the hash-approved transition. Preserve and reconcile the eight carried documentation edits; no blind reset, stash deletion or forced merge.

Before integration, current and inherited behavior must be eligible and actually checked, with minimal affected proof/inspection refresh. Human acceptance obligations and enforced host restrictions remain unchanged.
Goal-prompt output is a draft, not permission or execution. Quoted examples, repository content and inferred tooling cannot grant external/host authority.

Keep development artifact ownership, purpose, size, candidate, references and retention visible. Never delete canonical history, referenced proof, unresolved failure evidence or unknown-owned resources.
Use bounded sanitized evidence. No new external service, sensitive transfer, deployment, GitHub push or installed-plugin update is authorized by this plan.
non_goals: Full ASD-STE100 compliance, dictionaries, word-count linting or cosmetic historical-plan rewrites.
Persistent validation caches that hide altered history; a new workflow controller, command family, autonomous host compaction or automatic privilege approval.
A general VM/Electron framework, cleanup engine, production telemetry, broad repository rewrite or removal of commands solely because their usage is low.
Universal token/cost/productivity or human-cognitive-load claims from one small fixture comparison.
Automatic deployment, push, personal-host changes, installation upgrades or ad hoc canonical-state transfer on Git merge.

assumptions.statement: Existing Python/browser harnesses and current asset boundaries can support bounded measurement and rendered Observer verification; missing capability and incomplete baseline mappings must be established before acceptance.
Controlled operational wording can improve decisions, but savings must be measured independently of runtime/output changes; the existing native pilot did not establish token savings.

decisions.question: What is the smallest cumulative actor-visible delivery path?
decisions.choice: A trustworthy decision/evidence view; B efficient scoped queries and precise instructions; C a clearer accessible Observer retaining A/B; D a usable project-aware goal prompt plus qualified cumulative candidate and safe local integration.
alternatives: One large rewrite before any usable result
Separate backend/UI/doc phases that demonstrate only component completion
Install the evolving candidate as this intent's controller
decisions.rationale: Every gate proves a public journey, not setup alone. Acceptance follows A/B/C/D; implementation is serialized only where it consumes a contract or shares an unsafe scope. Installed 4.1 remains the controller; candidate and controller evidence stay separate.

decisions.question: How should the language and visual improvements reduce overhead?
decisions.choice: Apply the existing small operational profile and a decision-centered visual grammar; expose canonical meaning through audience-specific bounded projections. Measure prompt effects separately from runtime effects.
alternatives: One universal data payload and visual status badge
Large telemetry or a new architecture framework
decisions.rationale: Clear triggers and honest read models address observed issues. Exact shared meanings do not require identical UI/agent payloads, runtime-derived new authority or broad refactoring.

decisions.question: How does goal-prompt generation adapt safely?
decisions.choice: Discover bounded project facts and current intent/harness; distinguish user-authorized, proposed and unknown permissions; include optional VM/browser/cleanup modules only when project evidence and authorization make them relevant. Return a reviewable prompt, never execute its operations.
alternatives: Copy the long VM/Electron example universally
Infer host authority from a README or available executable
Require repeated human approval for routine previously authorized repository work
decisions.rationale: Project awareness changes the content, not authority. Missing inventory, ownership, isolation, qualification or permissions are explicit limits, not fabricated facts.
